excerpt: RecordMeeting records and transcribes Google Meet, Zoom and Teams calls without a bot joining, then gives AI notes and a share link. Pricing and alternatives.
content:
RecordMeeting is a meeting recorder that runs in your browser (as a Chrome extension or Google Workspace add-on) instead of sending a bot into the call. One click starts recording; afterwards you get the full video, a transcript, AI meeting notes and summaries, and a link to share with your team. Its site lists Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Webex, Telegram, WhatsApp and Discord, and you can chat with your recordings to find what was said.

Because no bot joins and other participants are not notified, the maker said on Product Hunt that the recording stays on your own machine and it is up to you to tell others you are recording. Call-recording laws differ by country and, in the US, by state: some places allow a call to be recorded with one participant's consent, while others require every participant's consent. Several commenters raised this and asked for a consent reminder. Check the rules that apply where you and each participant are before recording.

RecordMeeting is made by Qualtir, according to its site and its founder Nathan's Product Hunt comment. It launched on Product Hunt on 15 July 2026 and finished #9 for the day with 155 upvotes and 28 comments (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested RecordMeeting ourselves. This page brings together its official site and pricing page, its Product Hunt launch and the public pricing pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.platform: Chrome extension and Google Workspace add-on
profile.summary_short: Records and transcribes video calls without a bot joining the meeting

gallery.alt: RecordMeeting graphic 'Works with the meeting platforms you use': Google Meet, WhatsApp, Zoom, Discord, Webex, Teams and Telegram

paragraphs: Nathan, founder of Qualtir, says most AI notetakers still send a bot into your call, and the "Notetaker has joined" moment spoils sales calls, interviews and internal meetings.
RecordMeeting works with one click inside Google Meet, with no bot joining, and gives you the full video, a transcript and an AI summary after the call.

use_cases: Keeping notes of sales calls, customer interviews or hiring interviews
Recording internal stand-ups and sharing a summary link with the team
Searching past meetings by chatting with the recordings

fit: dislike notetaker bots joining your calls
mostly meet on Google Meet, Zoom or Teams from a browser
want a low-cost recorder with unlimited recordings
not_fit: work where every participant must consent to recording and you can't reliably tell everyone yourself
need team-wide policy controls on consent, which a commenter asked about and the launch did not offer

pricing.intro: RecordMeeting lists three plans; yearly billing saves 30%. Prices are in US dollars. Paid plans have a 30-day money-back guarantee.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: 5 unlocked recordings (older ones stay open, newer ones lock), recordings up to 1 hour, AI notes, full transcription, downloads, chat with recordings

plans.name: Pro
plans.detail: Unlimited recordings up to 6 hours each, AI notes, transcription, downloads, chat

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Everything in Pro plus organisations, folders, team management, shared billing and priority support

notes: At launch the maker said the free tier gave 20 recordings; the pricing page now says 5.

alternatives.intro: Other AI meeting notetakers. Prices are from each company's own pricing page on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Granola
items.what: AI meeting notes that work from your device without a bot joining
items.difference: Focused on notes rather than full video recordings.

items.name: Fathom
items.what: AI notetaker that records and summarises calls
items.starts_at: Free plan with unlimited recordings; Team $15/user/month billed annually
items.difference: Joins as a visible notetaker, which RecordMeeting avoids; its free plan has unlimited recordings.

asked: How privacy and consent work without a visible bot (it is up to the user to tell others)
How it differs from other recorders
Whether there is a time limit (1 hour on Free, 6 hours on paid plans, per the pricing page)
criticised: Several commenters noted that some places, including some US states, require every participant's consent to record a call, and suggested a consent reminder or announcement option

x.none: We found no posts about RecordMeeting on X yet.

faq.a: A browser-based meeting recorder that records and transcribes calls without a bot joining, then gives AI notes and a share link. It is made by Qualtir.
Free for 5 unlocked recordings of up to an hour. Pro is $9 a month and Enterprise $15 per seat a month, both billed yearly.

faq.q: Is it legal to record without telling people?
faq.a: It depends on where you and the other participants are. Some places allow a call to be recorded with one participant's consent; others require every participant's consent. RecordMeeting does not notify other participants, and the maker says telling them is up to you, so check the rules that apply before recording.

faq.q: Which platforms does it work with?
faq.a: Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Webex, Telegram, WhatsApp and Discord, according to its site.

faq.q: Is there a recording time limit?
faq.a: 1 hour per recording on Free and 6 hours on paid plans.
